Apple’s (NASDAQ:AAPL) Hold Rating Reaffirmed at Wells Fargo & Co Posted by Donna Armstrong | Jan 21st, 2018 
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) ‘s stock had its “hold” rating restated by analysts at Wells Fargo & Co in a research note issued to investors on Wednesday, December 27th. They currently have a $195.00 price objective on the iPhone maker’s stock. Wells Fargo & Co’s price objective indicates a potential upside of 9.27% from the company’s current price. 
AAPL has been the topic of several other reports. JPMorgan Chase & Co. reissued a “buy” rating and issued a price target on shares of Apple in a research note on Monday, September 11th. Robert W. Baird reissued a “buy” rating and issued a $172.00 price target on shares of Apple in a research note on Tuesday, September 5th. Drexel Hamilton restated a “buy” rating and set a $208.00 price objective on shares of Apple in a research report on Thursday, September 7th. Instinet restated a “buy” rating and set a $185.00 price objective (up from $175.00) on shares of Apple in a research report on Wednesday, September 6th. Finally, UBS Group restated a “buy” rating and set a $180.00 price objective on shares of Apple in a research report on Tuesday, August 29th. One research analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, eleven have issued a hold rating, thirty-eight have assigned a buy rating and one has assigned a strong buy rating to the stock. The stock has an average rating of “Buy” and an average target price of $200.59. Get Apple alerts: 
Shares of Apple ( NASDAQ:AAPL ) traded down $0.80 during midday trading on Wednesday, reaching $178.46. 30,827,809 shares of the company were exchanged, compared to its average volume of 25,680,000. Apple has a 12-month low of $119.50 and a 12-month high of $180.10. The stock has a market capitalization of $916,270.00, a P/E ratio of 19.42, a PEG ratio of 1.44 and a beta of 1.23. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.73, a current ratio of 1.28 and a quick ratio of 1.23. 
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last announced its quarterly earnings results on Thursday, November 2nd. The iPhone maker reported $2.07 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, topping the Zacks’ consensus estimate of $1.87 by $0.20. The firm had revenue of $52.58 billion for the quarter, compared to the consensus estimate of $50.71 billion. Apple had a net margin of 21.09% and a return on equity of 36.29%. The firm’s quarterly revenue was up 12.2% compared to the same quarter last year. During the same period in the prior year, the firm posted $1.50 earnings per share. equities analysts predict that Apple will post 11.15 earnings per share for the current fiscal year. 
In other news, insider Eduardo H. Cue sold 65,361 shares of the company’s stock in a transaction on Thursday, November 30th. The shares were sold at an average price of $171.60, for a total transaction of $11,215,947.60. The transaction was disclosed in a legal filing with the SEC, which can be accessed through the SEC website . Also, insider Daniel J. Riccio sold 15,641 shares of the company’s stock in a transaction on Friday, January 5th. The stock was sold at an average price of $174.78, for a total transaction of $2,733,733.98. Following the transaction, the insider now directly owns 13,739 shares in the company, valued at $2,401,302.42. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Over the last ninety days, insiders have sold 128,412 shares of company stock worth $22,115,155. Corporate insiders own 0.08% of the company’s stock. 
Several institutional investors have recently added to or reduced their stakes in the stock. Plancorp LLC lifted its holdings in Apple by 27.2% in the 4th quarter. Plancorp LLC now owns 18,183 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $3,082,000 after purchasing an additional 3,890 shares in the last quarter. Wealth Enhancement Advisory Services LLC lifted its holdings in Apple by 516.7% in the 4th quarter. Wealth Enhancement Advisory Services LLC now owns 36,018 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $6,378,000 after purchasing an additional 30,178 shares in the last quarter. Ingalls & Snyder LLC purchased a new position in Apple in the 4th quarter valued at about $29,116,000. Stokes & Hubbell Capital Management LLC lifted its holdings in Apple by 7.9% in the 4th quarter. Stokes & Hubbell Capital Management LLC now owns 70,698 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $11,964,000 after purchasing an additional 5,197 shares in the last quarter. Finally, TRUE Private Wealth Advisors lifted its holdings in Apple by 73.4% in the 4th quarter. TRUE Private Wealth Advisors now owns 44,669 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $7,559,000 after purchasing an additional 18,906 shares in the last quarter. Institutional investors and hedge funds own 60.19% of the company’s stock.
